question: How many cumulative autochthonous human West Nile virus cases in Île-de-France in 2026 will Santé publique France report in its bulletin covering data up to about 14 September 2026?

calls.reasoning: Anchor is 9 IdF autochthonous WNV cases at the 30 Aug 2026 cut-off (SPF bulletin of 2 Sept; national 39), confirmed by three independent press reports. The resolving bulletin (~16 Sept, cut-off ~14 Sept) is two accrual weeks later. Base rate from the 2025 SPF real-time trajectory: cumulative counts grew ~1.5-1.6x between the 31-Aug and 15-Sept cut-offs (national 20->32), giving ~14 from a base of 9. Upward pressure: national added +9 in the last observed week and IdF's 2026 onset curve started ~4-5 weeks earlier and broader than 2025's (virus in mosquito excreta in May, birds in four departments in June, five departments with human cases by late August); 2025 IdF ended at 18-19 despite showing only 3 in the 15-Sept-2025 bulletin, i.e. real confirmation lag adds cases for weeks after onset. Downward pressure: IdF added only +1 in the last week while the national +9 was concentrated in PACA/Occitanie, IdF's national share is falling (27% -> 23%), and the 2025 national onset peak was week 34 (18-24 Aug) so mid-September is well past peak. Evidence is decent on the anchor but thin on IdF-specific weekly increments (national bulletins report departments, not a regional count; the IdF regional PDFs would not parse), so I stay near the base-rate multiplier. Escape mass is small both ways: below 7.5 needs a downward reclassification (2025 IdF had 7 undifferentiated WNV/Usutu cases, so reclassification is a real mechanism) and above 35.5 needs +27 in two weeks, roughly a retrospective serology/blood-donor batch.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the Santé publique France 'surveillance renforcée' bulletin whose data cut-off falls in 8-14 Sept 2026 (national bulletins publish Wednesdays; the 16 Sept edition would carry a ~14 Sept cut-off), NOT off ARS Île-de-France press releases, NOT off news reports, NOT off the season-end bilan. Counts pure-WNV autochthonous human cases attributed to Île-de-France only; Usutu and undifferentiated WNV/Usutu categories are excluded. Note: recent 2026 NATIONAL bulletins state only 'Île-de-France (5 departments)' without a regional total — the region-level figure has been appearing in the SPF Île-de-France regional bulletin (published Thursdays: 21 Aug, 27 Aug, 4 Sept 2026), which the fine print permits as the source.

EVENT WINDOW: 1 May 2026 (start of enhanced surveillance, per the criteria) -> ~14 Sept 2026 bulletin cut-off; as of Now (2026-09-07T16:30Z), ~95% elapsed. Accrual window since the last observed data point: 30 Aug 2026 cut-off -> ~14 Sept 2026 cut-off, ~53% elapsed.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the count stands where the 2 Sept 2026 bulletin left it, i.e. no further Île-de-France cases are added over the two intervening bulletins.

EVIDENCE (2026):
- SPF bulletin 2 Sept 2026 (cut-off 30 Aug): 39 autochthonous WNV cases in mainland France, '+9 vs the previous week', across PACA (3 depts), Occitanie (4), Île-de-France (5), Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes (Drôme). For 2 cases no precise contamination site identified. (santepubliquefrance.fr; veille-acteurs-sante summary)
- Île-de-France reported series across 2026 bulletins: cut-off ~10 Aug = 0; ~17 Aug = 3 (2 Essonne, 1 Seine-Saint-Denis, 2 neuroinvasive, onsets back to mid-July); 24 Aug = 8 across five departments (Essonne 3, Seine-Saint-Denis 2, Val-de-Marne 1, Val-d'Oise 1, Seine-et-Marne 1 — first ever in Seine-et-Marne), 6 neuroinvasive; 30 Aug = 9. (SPF bulletins; Citoyens.com 3 Sept 2026)
- France 3 Île-de-France, 4 Sept 2026: 'une petite dizaine de cas ont été identifiés à ce stade' in the region, across five departments, against 39 nationally as of 30 Aug.
- PACA as of early Sept 2026: 18 autochthonous cases since early May, Bouches-du-Rhône worst hit with 9; press frames it as a Provence surge driven by repeated heatwaves. (press, ~4 Sept 2026)
- Non-human 2026 detections in Île-de-France: WNV in mosquito excreta (Val-de-Marne trap) in May 2026; ANSES national reference lab found 6 WNV-positive birds in 4 IdF departments (75, 77, 92, 94) in June 2026. Enhanced surveillance runs 1 May - 30 Nov. (ARS Île-de-France)
- Searched for but did NOT find: any bulletin with a cut-off after 30 Aug 2026; any Île-de-France departmental breakdown in the 2 Sept 2026 national bulletin; any 2026 Usutu or undifferentiated WNV/Usutu count for Île-de-France; any prediction market (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, bookmakers) pricing this quantity — none found; parseable text of the 4 Sept 2026 IdF regional bulletin PDF.

BASE RATES AND COMPARATORS:
- Class 'SPF real-time NATIONAL cumulative WNV counts by bulletin cut-off, 2025': 20 at 31 Aug -> 32 at 15 Sept -> 36 at 22 Sept -> 41 at 29 Sept -> 62 final for the season. The 31-Aug-to-15-Sept step is a factor of 1.60 (+12); the 15-Sept figure is 52% of the season final.
- Class 'SPF real-time ÎLE-DE-FRANCE cumulative counts, 2025' (first year of local transmission, weaker case-finding): ~2 at 31 Aug -> 3 at the 15 Sept cut-off -> 7 announced by ARS IdF on 19 Sept 2025 -> 18-19 in the season bilan. The 15-Sept figure was ~16% of the eventual regional total; the 19-Sept figure ~37%.
- Class 'Île-de-France season totals': 2025 = 19 autochthonous WNV (bilan; the national 2025 report states 18 across seven departments), plus 2 Usutu and 7 undifferentiated WNV/Usutu. Second most affected French region in 2025.
- Class 'France national season totals': 62 (2025, record), 38-39 (2024), 39 (2023), 6 (2022), 0 (2021).
- Onset seasonality, 2025 national: peak in ISO week 34 (18-24 Aug) with 12 cases, of which Île-de-France n=6, Occitanie n=4, PACA n=2. Of the 62 national 2025 cases, 20 (32%) were neuroinvasive and 5 (8%) died.
- 2026 Île-de-France observed week-on-week increments in the reported cumulative: +3, +5, +1.
- Reporting mechanics: SPF counts are by confirmation/report, not onset, and lag onset by weeks; 2025 Île-de-France figures rose substantially after mid-September through retrospective identification, so bulletin cumulatives are revised upward over the season (the criteria pin the first qualifying bulletin's figure).
- Peer-reviewed context: Emerg Infect Dis 31(11) documents two autochthonous Paris WNV encephalitis cases presenting 25 July and 2 Aug 2025, both residing near the Seine, framed as northward expansion.

DIRECTIONAL EVIDENCE BOTH WAYS — for further accrual: national count added 9 in the last observed week; five IdF departments already affected plus new departmental firsts (Seine-et-Marne); virus circulating in IdF since May with avian amplification in June; Culex activity in the region persists into late September; 2025 showed large post-mid-September additions to the IdF total. Against further accrual: the region added only 1 case in the last observed week while the national increase was concentrated in PACA/Occitanie; IdF's share of the national count fell from 8/30 to 9/39; the 2025 national onset curve peaked in week 34, so the mid-September window sits well past the modal onset week.
calls.reference_class: Santé publique France enhanced-surveillance real-time cumulative autochthonous WNV counts, 31-August cut-off to mid-September cut-off, French regions and nation 2025-2026

calls.reasoning: Anchor: the SPF bulletin series for Île-de-France in 2026 by data cut-off runs 0 (14 Aug) -> 3 (17 Aug) -> 8 (24 Aug) -> 9 (30 Aug), i.e. weekly increments +3, +5, +1, and the target bulletin (cut-off ~13 Sept) is two further weekly steps. Reference class: cumulative autochthonous WNV counts over the late-Aug-to-mid-Sept peak-reporting window in France; the national 2025 series went 20 (1 Sept) -> 23 (8 Sept) -> 36 (22 Sept), an interpolated ~1.45x over two weeks, which applied to 9 gives ~13 as the prior. Upward evidence: 2026 IdF onsets began mid-July (~2 weeks earlier than 2025's 31 July first case), five departments are already involved, national 2026 stood at 39 by the 30 Aug cut-off — above the whole 2025 national count at its 22 Sept cut-off — and 2025 IdF more than doubled (8 at 22 Sept to 19 final) through late-season accrual and retrospective ascertainment. Downward evidence: the most recent IdF weekly increment was the season's smallest (+1), Culex transmission and onsets in temperate France taper from mid-September, and the question excludes cases parked in the undifferentiated WNV/Usutu bucket (7 of 28 IdF flavivirus cases in 2025). I did not find any bulletin with a cut-off past 30 Aug, nor a 2026 IdF onset curve, so the last two weeks are extrapolation rather than observation — hence a wide, right-skewed distribution centred at 13. Escapes: ~2% below 8 via reclassification into the undifferentiated category or a downward-revised first figure; ~3% above 35, which would require quadrupling in two weeks (a large retrospective serological batch), more than the entire 2025 IdF season total.

calls.reference_class: Regional cumulative autochthonous West Nile virus case counts reported in weekly national surveillance bulletins over the late-August-to-mid-September peak-reporting window, in recently-affected temperate European regions — specifically Île-de-France 2025 and the France-hexagonale national series 20

calls.reasoning: Anchor: 9 IdF autochthonous WNV cases at the 30 Aug 2026 cut-off (SPF bulletin published 2 Sept), reached via weekly increments of +3, +5, +1. The target bulletin adds two more weekly cut-offs (~6 and ~13 Sept). Reference class of French regional WNV waves says mid-September is peak reporting (onset peak late Aug + 2-3 week confirmation lag), implying growth of roughly 1.3-1.7x over such a two-week window, i.e. ~12-15. The single +1 week is a genuine damper suggesting IdF onsets (mid-July onward) may have peaked early, which is why I keep material mass at 10-11; conversely EFS donor-screening and serology batches can land several cases at once, giving a right tail to ~21. A 2025-shape season (IdF 18-19 total) with 2026 running ~3 weeks ahead puts mid-September at roughly 55-70% of an eventual ~20-25, again ~13-16. Downside is floored at 9 (cumulative counts do not fall); upside past 35 would need +27 in two weeks, priced at 1%. No prediction market exists on this or any near-miss contract, so no crowd anchor.

- Over all French seasons 2018-2025 (national autochthonous WNV, SPF): 2018 = 27, 2023 = 39, 2024 = 38, 2025 = 62 (record).
- Over the single prior IdF season (2025, first-ever local transmission there): 18 autochthonous WNV cases across 7 departments per the SPF national 2025 bilan (the SPF IdF regional bilan states 19), plus 2 autochthonous Usutu and 7 undifferentiated WNV/Usutu; case identification spanned 31 July - 30 Nov 2025; departmental spread reported as Seine-Saint-Denis 8, Val-de-Marne 7, Hauts-de-Seine 5, Paris 2 (this breakdown appears to span all flavivirus categories, not WNV alone).

- National 2025 cumulative by bulletin cut-off (same reporting instrument as this question): 8 Sept = 23; 15 Sept = 32; 22 Sept = 36; season end = 62. Two-week increment across 8->22 Sept 2025 = +13 on a base of 23 (1.57x).

SERIES SPREAD (observed weekly changes, IdF 2026 cumulative, the only in-region series available): +3, +5, +1 over the three reporting weeks to ~16/23/30 Aug 2026. National 2026 weekly change to 30 Aug: +9.

EVIDENCE POINTING BOTH WAYS: 2026 IdF reached 9 by 30 Aug versus roughly 2-3 at the same calendar date in 2025, and spread to a new department (77), so the regional wave is larger and earlier than the prior season; national 2026 at 30 Aug (39) already exceeds the 2025 figure at 15 Sept (32). calls.reasoning: Anchor is 9 IdF autochthonous WNV cases at the 30 Aug 2026 cut-off (SPF bulletin of 2 Sept; national 39), agreed by all three runs and corroborated by regional press with a five-department breakdown. The resolving bulletin (~16 Sept, cut-off ~13-14 Sept) is two accrual weeks later. The reconciled 2025 national series by cut-off is 20 (1 Sept) -> 23 (8 Sept) -> 32 (15 Sept) -> 36 (22 Sept) -> 62 final, a 1.60x two-week step across exactly this window; applied to 9 that gives ~14.4, and mid-September is when late-August onsets clear the 2-4 week serological lag. Upward: 2026 IdF is running ~3-4 weeks ahead of 2025 (9 by 30 Aug vs ~2), five departments involved including a first-ever case in Seine-et-Marne, national 2026 at 39 by 30 Aug already exceeds 2025's 22-Sept figure, and EFS donor screening reports in batches. Downward: the last observed IdF increment was the season's smallest (+1) while the national +9 sat in PACA/Occitanie, IdF's national share is falling, and the question excludes the undifferentiated WNV/Usutu bucket that absorbed 7 of 28 IdF flavivirus cases in 2025. calls.reconciliation: In dispute: (a) the national 2025 cumulative at the 15 Sept cut-off — Runs 1 and 3 independently observed 32, Run 2 interpolated ~29-30 and derived a 1.45x multiplier; I take 32 (two direct observations beat one interpolation), which raises the reference-class centre from ~13 to ~14.4 and is the main reason my median sits above the runs'. (b) The 2025 IdF figures at the same calendar point (3 at the 15 Sept cut-off per Run 1; 7 per ARS on 19 Sept and 8 at the 22 Sept cut-off per Runs 2/3) are compatible different instruments and jointly document steep late-September retrospective ascertainment. (c) IdF 2025 season total 18 (national bilan) vs 19 (regional bilan) could not be settled without web access and is immaterial here. (d) Pure judgment, unbroken by evidence: whether the single +1 week means the IdF wave crested. I read it as Poisson noise on a ~3/week rate in a five-department region rather than a regime change, so it fattens my left tail (p10=10, i.e. only +1 over two weeks) without moving the centre below the base rate — that is the reading I would bet on. (e) Escape below 7.5: Run 3 priced none, Runs 1/2 priced 2%; reclassification into the undifferentiated WNV/Usutu category is a documented mechanism (7 of 28 IdF flavivirus cases in 2025), so I keep 2%. Upper escape needs +27 in two weeks, more than the entire 2025 IdF season, priced at 1.5%. No web retrieval on this run; no prediction market on this or any near-miss contract was found by any run, so there is no crowd anchor to blend.
